title.narrative: Pillar I - Providing a package of services to PwDs and Older persons in the prioritized cadasters of Akkar and Tripoli.

description.narrative:
ltpgtltbrgt
lt/pgtltp style="margin-left:.5in" class="MsoNormal"gtltspan style="line-height: 107% color: black"gtLebanon is currently facing its most severe economic recession in its history, exacerbated by a series of crises including the Syrian refugee influx, street protests, COVID-19 pandemic, resource depletion, and the devastating Beirut port explosion in August 2020. These overlapping economic, financial, and social challenges have pushed Lebanon to the brink of collapse. The country's economic crisis is ranked among the top ten most severe globally, with a drastic depreciation of the Lebanese lira and triple-digit annual inflation. As a result, living standards have deteriorated, and the well-being of the population has significantly worsened. Food insecurity and limited access to basic services have become widespread across all population groups. ltbrgtThis project specifically targets persons with disabilities (PwDs) and older persons from all population groups who face heightened vulnerabilities, including socioeconomic vulnerability, food insecurity, increased protection threats, and lack of critical assistive devices and specialized therapies. A key focus of the project is addressing period poverty among women and girls with disabilities, by improving their access to menstrual hygiene products. This will reduce stress and anxiety levels and prevent complications such as allergies and infections. ltbrgtTo address the urgent needs and challenges faced by the targeted population, the project will provide a comprehensive package of tailored services through an integrated approach. This includes distributing 2,400 nutritionally balanced food parcels to 300 households over 8 months, providing 600 menstrual hygiene kits to 150 women and girls with disabilities over 4 months, and conducting three awareness sessions on menstrual health and hygiene for 150 women and girls. Additionally, the project encompasses the provision of 100 home care supplies, and 600 physical therapy sessions for 40 PwDs and older persons. The selection of eligible beneficiaries will be based on a validation assessment, which will be reviewed by the donor prior to the implementation phase. The project will target ltbgthouseholds with at least one person with a disability or an older person, with priority given to households with member with complex and/or severe disabilities as they have higher level of vulnerability and gaps in meeting basic needs.lt/bgtlt/spangtltspan style="line-height: 107% font-family: Arial, sans-serif color: black"gtlt/spangtlt/pgt
